mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate at or below 0.25% indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower financing costs.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in unemployment rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending capacity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% in one month indicate broad-based consumer demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in 1 month (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%) and persistently low interest rates (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25%), the market anticipates aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained industrial production decline below 100 (index 2017=100) indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output capacity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly real GDP decline exceeding 0.5% year-over-year signals economic contraction that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 YoY decline > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high unemployment (UNRATE > 9.5%) and declining employment (PAYEMS < 130,000) indicate severe labor market stress that reduces consumer spending power, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 9.5% and PAYEMS < 130000 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained housing starts level above 650 (thousands of units) indicates strong consumer demand for housing, which correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased construction activity and consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 650 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).
